How Solar Works

## Your Roof Turns Sunlight Into Savings

Panels on your roof make electricity from sunlight; the inverter makes it usable for your fans, lights and appliances; and any extra power goes to the grid through net metering, earning you credit on your bill.

1

### Panels

Solar panels on your roof turn sunlight into clean DC electricity.

2

### Inverter

The inverter converts it to AC power for your fans, lights, fridge and appliances.

3

### Net Meter

Surplus power goes to the grid and is credited against the units you draw at night.

4

### You Save

Lower bills from the first month, and largely free power for 25 years and more.

FAQ

## Your Solar Questions, Answered

Everything you need to know before going solar with Lotus Sun Energy.

How much does rooftop solar cost for a home?

A typical home system costs about **₹55,000 to ₹65,000 per kW** before subsidy. After the PM Surya Ghar subsidy (up to ₹78,000), most homes pay back the cost in roughly **3 to 5 years** and then enjoy largely free power for 25 years and more. Try our savings calculator for your numbers.

What government subsidy can I get?

Under **PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana**, homes get ₹30,000 per kW for the first 2 kW and ₹18,000 for the 3rd kW, up to **₹78,000**. Housing societies get ₹18,000 per kW for common facilities. We handle the whole application for you. [Read the subsidy guide](https://lotussunenergy.com/pm-surya-ghar-subsidy/).

Is my roof suitable for solar?

Most are. You generally need about **80 to 100 sq ft of shade-free roof per kW**. During our free site visit we check the roof area, direction, shade and your usage, then recommend the right size.

Can I pay in EMIs?

Yes. Banks offer solar loans, and home systems up to 3 kW can get collateral-free loans at around 7% under the scheme. In many cases your EMI is close to your current bill, so you save from day one.

How long does installation take?

Once the DISCOM feasibility is approved, the physical installation usually takes just **2 to 4 days** for a home rooftop.

What about maintenance and the monsoon?

Solar needs very little maintenance: rinse the panels every few weeks and get a yearly check-up. Panels still generate on cloudy days (at lower output), and **net metering** lets you bank surplus summer power against monsoon months.

Do you also do commercial and ground-mount solar?

Yes. Besides homes, we design and build rooftop systems for shops, offices, schools and factories, and ground-mount plants on open land, including piling, civil works, fencing and maintenance.

Why choose a veteran-led solar company?

Lotus Sun Energy is led by ex-servicemen. That means **discipline, careful planning, strict safety and keeping our word** on every site, with honest advice instead of pushy sales.

[More Questions & Answers](https://lotussunenergy.com/faq/)

India has committed to 500 GW of non-fossil power capacity by 2030 and to net zero by 2070 (see [India's climate commitments](https://lotussunenergy.com/solar-schemes-india/#panchamrit)). Quality & Safety

# Built Right, Built Safe

How we make sure every solar system we build is safe, compliant and ready to perform for 25 years: certified equipment, Indian standards, careful workmanship and full testing.

Our Standards

## What we check on every job

Solar is electrical work on roofs and in the open, designed to run unattended for decades. Quality and safety are not extras: they are the job. These are the standards we build to. For the detail behind them, read our guide to [solar standards in India](https://lotussunenergy.com/solar-quality-standards-bis-cea/).

### Certified equipment

- Modules on MNRE's ALMM list and carrying the BIS mark, as the Quality Control Order requires
- Indian-made (DCR) modules where the PM Surya Ghar subsidy or a scheme needs them
- BIS-certified inverters with the protection functions your DISCOM requires
- Make, model and serial numbers recorded and matched to the documents on delivery

### Sound design

- Structure designed for your area's wind speed and your roof's strength
- Shade analysis so every panel gets the sun
- Cables sized for low losses, with DC and AC protection in proper distribution boards
- Earthing and lightning protection to the relevant Indian standards and CEA safety regulations

### Safe installation

- Safe working at height: harnesses, ladders and edge protection
- Neat cable routing in conduit or trays, properly crimped MC4 connectors
- Isolation and lock-out before any electrical work
- Site cleaned and left safe at the end of every day

### Testing and handover

- Insulation resistance, polarity, open-circuit voltage and earth-resistance tests
- Inverter settings checked and grid synchronisation verified
- DISCOM inspection and, for larger plants, the electrical inspector's (CEIG) approval
- Handover file: test reports, warranties, approvals, single-line diagram and care guide

## Standards We Follow

Modules: **ALMM List-I, BIS mark**

Inverters: **BIS certified**

Safety: **CEA regulations**

Subsidy systems: **DCR modules**

How It Works

# Going Solar, Step by Step

How solar makes power for your home or business, and every step of going solar with Lotus Sun Energy, from the free site visit to the day your bill drops.

[Get a Free Quote](https://lotussunenergy.com/free-solar-quote/)[Estimate My Savings](https://lotussunenergy.com/#calculator)

The Basics

## How Solar Makes Power

1

### Panels capture sunlight

Solar cells turn sunlight into DC electricity. In most of India, 1 kW of panels makes about 4 units a day on average.

2

### The inverter converts it

The inverter turns DC into the AC power your fans, lights, fridge and machines use, and matches it to the grid.

3

### You use it first

Solar power feeds your own loads first, so you buy fewer units from the DISCOM during the day.

4

### Surplus goes to the grid

With net metering, extra units are exported and credited against what you draw at night or on cloudy days.

Working With Us

## From First Call to Switch-On

For a typical home: about 2 to 4 days of work on site, and a few weeks in all, depending on your DISCOM.

- 1

**Enquiry**

Send us a message or fill in the free quote form with your location and a recent bill. We call you back within one working day.

- 2

**Free site visit**

We check the roof or land, shade, structure, wiring and sanctioned load, and answer all your questions.

- 3

**Design and quotation**

A system sized to your use, a generation and savings estimate, named makes, and one all-inclusive price with GST and subsidy shown.

- 4

**Registration and feasibility**

For homes we register you on the PM Surya Ghar portal; for every grid-connected system we apply to the DISCOM for feasibility and net metering.

- 5

**Installation**

Structure, panels, inverter, earthing, lightning protection and wiring, installed neatly and safely.

- 6

**Net meter, inspection and commissioning**

The DISCOM fits the bi-directional meter and inspects the system; we commission it and hand over the documents.

- 7

**Subsidy credited**

For homes, we follow up the subsidy claim until it reaches your bank account.

- 8

**Support**

Monitoring, cleaning advice, yearly check-ups and help whenever you need it.

Who Owns What

## Clear From Day One

 | Item | Who |
| --- | --- |
  | The solar system | You, from the day it is installed (CAPEX model) |
 | The subsidy (homes) | Credited directly to your bank account by the government |
 | Equipment warranties | In your name, from the manufacturers; we hand over the certificates |
 | Installation workmanship | Lotus Sun Energy, as written in your contract |
 | The net meter | Installed and owned by your DISCOM |

# Rooftop Solar in Muzaffarpur & Bihar

A Bihar-based, veteran-led solar company: rooftop solar for homes and businesses from our office in Muzaffarpur, with the PM Surya Ghar subsidy, DISCOM approvals and net metering handled for you.

[Book a Free Site Visit](https://lotussunenergy.com/free-solar-quote/)[Estimate My Savings](https://lotussunenergy.com/#calculator)

Local, Not Far Away

## Solar from a team that lives here

Lotus Sun Energy is based at Pakhanaha Sriram in Muzaffarpur. We know Bihar's homes, roofs, weather and DISCOM processes, and we are close enough to visit your site, install carefully and come back whenever you need us.

Bihar is well suited to solar: most of the state receives roughly 4.5 to 5 kWh of sunlight per square metre per day, so 1 kW of panels typically makes about 4 units a day averaged over the year. With domestic tariffs rising and power cuts still common in many areas, a rooftop system (with batteries if you want backup) pays back quickly.

### Who looks after what in Bihar

- **NBPDCL** (North Bihar Power Distribution Company) serves north Bihar, including Muzaffarpur, Vaishali, Darbhanga, Samastipur, Sitamarhi and the Champarans
- **SBPDCL** (South Bihar Power Distribution Company) serves south Bihar, including Patna, Gaya, Bhagalpur, Nalanda and Bhojpur
- Your DISCOM checks feasibility, installs the net meter and inspects the system; we prepare and file the paperwork
- Home subsidy applications go through the national portal, pmsuryaghar.gov.in, and the subsidy is paid to your bank account
- **BREDA** (Bihar Renewable Energy Development Agency) is the state's nodal agency for renewable energy

### Designed for Bihar's weather

- Raised structures and good drainage for heavy monsoon rain and waterlogged areas
- Wind-rated mounting for pre-monsoon storms
- Proper earthing and lightning protection: the state sees frequent lightning
- Cleaning plans for the dusty months before the monsoon
- Hybrid inverters with batteries where power cuts are frequent

**हिंदी में:** लोटस सन एनर्जी मुजफ्फरपुर (बिहार) की पूर्व सैनिकों द्वारा संचालित सोलर कंपनी है। हम घरों और दुकानों के लिए रूफटॉप सोलर लगाते हैं, पीएम सूर्य घर योजना की सब्सिडी (₹78,000 तक), नेट मीटरिंग और सभी कागज़ी काम खुद संभालते हैं। मुफ्त साइट विज़िट के लिए संपर्क करें।

FAQ

## Solar in Bihar: Common Questions

Does the PM Surya Ghar subsidy apply in Bihar?

Yes. PM Surya Ghar is a central scheme available across India, including Bihar: ₹30,000 for 1 kW, ₹60,000 for 2 kW and ₹78,000 for 3 kW or more for a home. Ask us whether any state top-up is available when you apply; we will tell you the current position.

Which DISCOM handles net metering in Muzaffarpur?

Muzaffarpur is served by NBPDCL (North Bihar Power Distribution Company). We file the feasibility and net-metering application with NBPDCL, or with SBPDCL if you are in south Bihar.

Is solar worth it in Bihar with the monsoon?

Yes. Output dips on cloudy monsoon days, but the sunny months more than make up for it, and net metering lets you bank summer surplus against the monsoon. Over a year, 1 kW typically produces around 1,400 to 1,500 units.

Can I get backup during power cuts?

A standard on-grid system shuts down during a grid outage for safety. For backup, choose a hybrid system with batteries; we will show you the difference in cost honestly.

Where is your office?

Pakhanaha Sriram, Muzaffarpur, Bihar 843109. We are open Monday to Saturday, 9 AM to 7 PM, and offer free site visits across Bihar.

# Rooftop Solar, Made Simple for Your Family

From an independent house to a housing society, we design the right solar system for your roof, your usage and your budget, and handle everything end to end.

What We Do

## Turn your roof into a power plant

Your roof sits in the sun all day. Rooftop solar puts that free sunlight to work: it generates clean electricity for your home, cuts your monthly bill and protects you from ever-rising tariffs. With the [PM Surya Ghar subsidy](https://lotussunenergy.com/pm-surya-ghar-subsidy/) and easy EMIs, it is more affordable than most families expect.

No running around government offices or chasing vendors. From your first question to long-term service, Lotus Sun Energy takes care of it all, so you can simply enjoy the savings.

- Free site visit, shade check and an honest recommendation
- System sized to your bill and sanctioned load
- Indian-made (DCR) modules where the subsidy needs them, with warranties in writing

Bills around ₹2,500 to ₹4,500 a month. The most popular size, and it gets the full ₹78,000 subsidy.

**5 kW+**Large homes

Bills above ₹5,000 a month, or homes with ACs and pumps. Sized to your use for bigger savings.

FAQ

## Frequently Asked Questions

What size solar system does my home need?

As a guide: bills of ₹1,000 to ₹2,500 a month suit 1 to 2 kW, ₹2,500 to ₹4,500 suit about 3 kW (which also gets the full ₹78,000 subsidy), and bills above ₹5,000 need 5 kW or more. We confirm the size from your bills and roof on the free site visit.

How much subsidy will I get?

₹30,000 for 1 kW, ₹60,000 for 2 kW and ₹78,000 for 3 kW or more under PM Surya Ghar. The subsidy is credited to your bank account after the system is installed and inspected.

Will I still have power during a power cut?

A standard on-grid system switches off during a grid outage for safety. If you want backup, we can fit a hybrid inverter with batteries; we will show you the extra cost honestly.

Can I pay in EMIs?

Yes. Banks offer solar loans, and home systems up to 3 kW can get collateral-free loans at around 7% under the scheme. The EMI is often close to the bill it replaces.

Own Your Solar Plant

# Own Your Solar Plant: CAPEX Solar

Pay for your solar system once, upfront or through a loan, and own it from day one. We design, supply, install and commission it; every unit it makes is yours.

What We Do

## What the CAPEX model means for you

Under the CAPEX (capital expenditure) model you buy the solar system outright. There is no long-term power purchase agreement and no developer margin on every unit: the savings, the subsidy (for homes) and the depreciation (for businesses) are all yours.

For most homes and businesses this gives the lowest lifetime cost of power. If paying upfront is a stretch, a solar loan or EMI spreads the cost, often for about what you pay the DISCOM today. Read our [CAPEX vs OPEX guide](https://lotussunenergy.com/capex-vs-opex-solar/) for the full comparison.

### What's Included

- Free site visit and load study
- System design and generation estimate
- Supply of BIS-certified, ALMM-listed modules and warrantied inverters
- Structures, installation, earthing and testing
- Subsidy, net metering and approvals
- Commissioning and handover with all documents
- Optional maintenance plan

## At a Glance

Ownership: **Yours from day one**

Payment: **Upfront or EMI / loan**

Benefits: **Subsidy (homes), depreciation (business)**

Contract: **No PPA, no lock-in**

[CAPEX vs OPEX solar](https://lotussunenergy.com/capex-vs-opex-solar/)[Accelerated depreciation](https://lotussunenergy.com/accelerated-depreciation-solar/)[GST on solar](https://lotussunenergy.com/gst-on-solar-india/)

FAQ

## Frequently Asked Questions

What is the CAPEX model for solar?

You pay for the system and own it from day one. We design, supply, install and commission it; every unit it generates is yours, with no long-term power purchase agreement.

Is CAPEX better than OPEX?

Usually yes over 25 years, because you do not pay a developer's margin on every unit. OPEX avoids the upfront cost but locks you into a long contract. We will compare both honestly for your site.

Can I still pay monthly?

Yes. A bank solar loan or EMI lets you own the system while spreading the cost; for homes up to 3 kW, the scheme offers collateral-free loans at around 7%.

# Rooftop Solar

On-grid rooftop solar for homes, housing societies, shops, offices, schools and factories, turning unused roof space into a clean, bill-cutting power source.

What We Do

## Rooftop solar, done properly

From RCC terraces to large metal-sheet sheds, we design rooftop systems that make the most of your roof while protecting it. We check the structure and the shade, choose the right mounting, liaise with your DISCOM for net metering and commission the system safely.

A rooftop system uses space you already own, so there is no land, fencing or piling cost, and the power is used right where it is made. For homes the [PM Surya Ghar subsidy](https://lotussunenergy.com/pm-surya-ghar-subsidy/) applies; for businesses, [accelerated depreciation](https://lotussunenergy.com/accelerated-depreciation-solar/) and [5% GST](https://lotussunenergy.com/gst-on-solar-india/) help the numbers.

- Leak-proof mounting for RCC and metal-sheet roofs
- Elevated structures where you want to use the terrace below
- Net-metering and DISCOM liaison
- BIS-certified modules and on-grid or hybrid inverters
- Walkways, earthing and lightning protection
- Generation monitoring on your phone

From a 1 kW home system to large rooftops on factory sheds. Size is limited by your shade-free roof area and your sanctioned load.

# Ground-Mount Solar

Solar plants on open land for farms, factories, institutions and captive use: designed, built and connected to the grid by one veteran-led team.

What We Do

## Solar on your land

Where the roof is too small or unsuitable, open land makes a superb solar site. Ground-mount plants can face the sun at the ideal angle, are easy to clean and maintain, and can be sized well beyond what a roof allows.

Solar Service

# Pile Foundation & Piling

Solar pile foundations designed for your soil: so ground-mount structures stay level and firm through monsoon floods and storms for 25 years and more.

What We Do

## Foundations that last the life of the plant

A ground-mount plant is only as good as its foundations. The right pile depends on the soil, the water table and the wind loads of your area, so we start with a soil check and design the piles to suit, rather than using one size for every site.

We set out the rows accurately, auger or drive the piles, cast them with proper concrete and curing, and test a sample for pull-out strength before the structures go up.

### What's Included

- Soil investigation and pile design
- Survey and setting-out of rows
- Augered cast-in-situ piles or driven steel piles
- Concrete mix control and cube tests
- Pile-cap and foundation bolt alignment
- Pull-out and lateral load tests
- Records for every pile

## At a Glance

Pile types: **Augered RCC or driven steel**

Design basis: **Soil report & wind zone**

Tests: **Cube, pull-out, lateral**

Suits: **All ground-mount plants**

## Planning a project?

Book a free site visit with our veteran-led team: no cost, no obligation.

[Get a Free Quote](https://lotussunenergy.com/free-solar-quote/)

## Read More

[Rooftop vs ground-mount](https://lotussunenergy.com/rooftop-vs-ground-mount-solar/)[Solar standards in India](https://lotussunenergy.com/solar-quality-standards-bis-cea/)

FAQ

## Frequently Asked Questions

Why does a solar plant need pile foundations?

Piles anchor the mounting structures so they resist wind uplift and stay level on soft or flood-prone ground for the life of the plant.

Augered or driven piles: which is better?

It depends on the soil. Augered cast-in-situ piles suit most Indian soils; driven steel piles are faster where the soil allows. The soil test decides.

Do you test the piles?

Yes: concrete cube tests and pull-out and lateral load tests on sample piles, with the results handed over.

Solar Service

# Civil Works & Fencing

All the civil works a solar plant needs: foundations, cable trenches, inverter rooms, internal roads, drainage, boundary walls and chain-link fencing.

What We Do

## The groundwork behind a good plant

Good civil work keeps a solar plant dry, secure and easy to maintain. Poor drainage, weak trenches or a sagging fence cause problems for years, so we plan the civil scope together with the electrical design.

We can take the civil package on its own for a developer or EPC company, or as part of a complete ground-mount plant.

### What's Included

- Foundations for inverters, transformers, ACDB and control rooms
- Cable trenches, conduits and road crossings
- Earth-pit chambers and covers
- Internal roads and walkways
- Storm-water drainage
- Pre-cast or brick boundary walls
- Chain-link fencing and gates

## At a Glance

Scope: **Foundations to fencing**

Works for: **Owners, EPCs, developers**

Quality checks: **Cube tests, levels, alignment**

Suits: **Ground-mount & rooftop plants**

FAQ

## Frequently Asked Questions

What civil works does a solar plant need?

Equipment foundations, cable trenches, earth pits, internal roads, drainage and a secure boundary with fencing and gates. Rooftop systems need far less: mainly bases for the structures and inverters.

Can you do only the civil works?

Yes. We can take the civil and fencing package alone for a developer or EPC company.

Which fencing do you recommend?

Chain-link fencing on concrete posts is the usual choice for solar plants; pre-cast walls suit sites that need more security.

Solar Service

# O&M & Support

Operation and maintenance that keeps your solar system at peak output: cleaning, inspections, inverter checks, fault response and generation reports.

What We Do

## Keep every panel earning

Dust, bird droppings, loose connections and a tripped inverter can quietly eat into your savings. A simple maintenance plan catches these early, so the system keeps producing what it should for 25 years.

We offer maintenance for systems we install and for existing systems installed by others, from a yearly check-up for a home to a full O&M contract for a commercial or ground-mount plant. Read our [O&M and module cleaning guide](https://lotussunenergy.com/solar-om-module-cleaning/).

### What's Included

- Scheduled module cleaning or cleaning-team training
- Visual and thermal inspection of modules and connections
- Inverter health checks and firmware updates
- Earthing and lightning-protection tests
- Monitoring of generation against expectation
- Fault response and warranty claims
- Monthly or yearly generation reports

## At a Glance

Plans: **Yearly check-up to full O&M**

Systems: **Ours and others'**

Reports: **Generation & faults**

Response: **Quick on-call support**

FAQ

## Frequently Asked Questions

How often should solar panels be cleaned?

Usually every 2 to 4 weeks, more often in dusty, dry months and less in the monsoon. Use plain water and a soft brush or mop, early in the morning.

Do you maintain systems installed by other companies?

Yes. We start with an inspection and a report on the system's condition, then suggest a plan.

How do I know my system is performing well?

Compare its monthly generation with the expected figure for your size and location. We set up monitoring and flag any drop.

Solar Schemes & Policies

# Government Solar Schemes in India

What the Government of India offers for solar in 2026, from the PM Surya Ghar home subsidy to PM-KUSUM, GST and net metering, with every figure linked to its official source.

India's Solar Push

## The National Picture

Figures from PIB and MNRE data, each linked to its source. Updated October 2026.

[500  GWNon-fossil capacity target for 2030: the first of the Prime Minister's Panchamrit commitments at COP26Source: PIB](https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1768712)[283.46  GWNon-fossil capacity installed in India as on 31 March 2026Source: PIB](https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2250039)[50 %Share of India's installed power capacity from non-fossil sources, reached June 2025Source: PIB](https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2250039)[164.59  GWSolar capacity installed in India as on 31 July 2026 (MNRE data)Source: MNRE data](https://solarquarter.com/2026/08/12/indias-solar-capacity-surpasses-164-gw-as-2026-installations-approach-29-gw-by-july-end/)[75  lakhHouseholds targeted for rooftop solar under PM Surya Ghar by December 2026, on the way to 1 croreSource: PIB](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2268992)

Panchamrit

## India's Five Climate Commitments

Announced by the Prime Minister at COP26 in Glasgow. Every solar system built in India counts towards them.

- 1

India will reach its non-fossil energy capacity to 500 GW by 2030.

- 2

India will meet 50 percent of its energy requirements from renewable energy by 2030.

- 3

India will reduce the total projected carbon emissions by one billion tonnes from now onwards till 2030.

- 4

By 2030, India will reduce the carbon intensity of its economy by less than 45 percent.

- 5

By the year 2070, India will achieve the target of Net Zero.

The five commitments in the Prime Minister's words, from his national statement at COP26, Glasgow, 1 November 2021 ([PIB](https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1768712)).

Schemes & Policies

## Schemes That Matter for Solar

Every central scheme, tax rule and norm that shapes a solar system in India, as of October 2026: who it is for, the key points, its status, how we help, and a full guide on each.

| Scheme or policy | For | Status (Oct 2026) | In depth |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana | Homes & housing societies | Open; apply on pmsuryaghar.gov.in | Guide |
| PM-KUSUM | Farmers, cooperatives, panchayats, FPOs | Closing: complete by 31 Mar 2027 | Guide |
| Accelerated depreciation | Businesses that own their plant | Available to business owners | Guide |
| GST on solar at 5% | Everyone buying a solar plant | In force | Guide |
| Net metering and time-of-day tariffs | Grid-connected consumers | In force; 2026 changes in draft | Guide |
| Green Energy Open Access | Consumers of 100 kW and more | In force; state charges vary | Guide |
| ALMM List-I and List-II | Projects covered by the ALMM order | In force from 1 June 2026 | Guide |
| Customs duty on modules and cells | Anyone importing equipment | In force | Guide |
| BIS Quality Control Order | Every plant: modules, inverters, batteries | In force | Guide |
| Storage with solar | Utility tenders and large prosumers | Advisory for future tenders | Guide |

Homes & housing societies

### PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana

Open; apply on pmsuryaghar.gov.in

- Launched on 13 February 2024; approved by the Union Cabinet on 29 February 2024 with an outlay of Rs 75,021 crore
- Central subsidy: Rs 30,000 for 1 kW, Rs 60,000 for 2 kW and Rs 78,000 for 3 kW or more
- Housing societies and RWAs: Rs 18,000 per kW for common facilities, up to 500 kW
- Collateral-free loans of around 7% for home systems up to 3 kW; Indian-made (DCR) modules and a registered vendor required
- Target: 75 lakh households by December 2026, on the way to 1 crore

**Where we fit:** We register you on the national portal, file the DISCOM feasibility and net-metering papers, install a DCR-compliant system and follow the subsidy claim to your bank account.

[Read the full guide](https://lotussunenergy.com/pm-surya-ghar-subsidy/)[Source: PIB](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2268992)

Farmers, cooperatives, panchayats, FPOs

### PM-KUSUM

Closing: complete by 31 Mar 2027

- Component A: grid-connected solar plants of 500 kW to 2 MW on farmers' land, power bought by the DISCOM
- Component B: standalone solar pumps, with 30% central support (50% in the North-East, hill states and islands) plus state support
- Component C: solarisation of grid-connected pumps, individually or by whole feeders
- Financial closure for Components A and C extended to 30 November 2026; completion by 31 March 2027, with no further extension
- PM-KUSUM 2.0, with about 10 GW for agri-photovoltaics, announced but not yet notified

**Where we fit:** Component A and feeder-level plants are ground-mount plants: we can design and build them, including piling, fencing, civil works, installation and commissioning.

[Read the full guide](https://lotussunenergy.com/pm-kusum-scheme/)[Source: Energetica India](https://energetica-india.net/news/mnre-extends-pm-kusum-financial-closure-deadline-to-nov-30)

Businesses that own their plant

### Accelerated depreciation

Available to business owners

- Solar power generating systems are depreciated at 40% a year on the written-down value
- The Income-tax Act, 2025 applies from 1 April 2026; the 40% rate for qualifying solar assets is reported to continue
- Half the year's depreciation if the plant is used for less than 180 days in its first year

**Where we fit:** Every plant we build on the CAPEX model belongs to the client, so the depreciation is theirs. Confirm the position with your chartered accountant.

[Read the full guide](https://lotussunenergy.com/accelerated-depreciation-solar/)[Source: Taxguru: Income-tax Act, 2025](https://taxguru.in/income-tax/depreciation-income-tax-act-2025-section-34-rates-provisions.html)

Everyone buying a solar plant

### GST on solar at 5%

In force

- The 56th GST Council cut GST on solar cells, modules and specified devices from 12% to 5%, effective 22 September 2025
- EPC contracts: 70% goods at 5% and 30% services at 18%, about 8.9% overall
- The Andhra Pradesh High Court upheld the 70:30 method for a solar EPC contract in December 2025

**Where we fit:** We set out supply and services clearly in every quotation, so the tax treatment is transparent from the start.

[Read the full guide](https://lotussunenergy.com/gst-on-solar-india/)[Source: pv magazine India, 4 Sep 2025](https://www.pv-magazine-india.com/2025/09/04/gst-on-solar-cells-modules-cut-to-5/)

Grid-connected consumers

### Net metering and time-of-day tariffs

In force; 2026 changes in draft

- Net metering up to 500 kW or the sanctioned load, whichever is lower, under the national consumer rules; states set the details
- Above that, net billing or gross metering
- Time-of-day tariffs make solar hours cheaper and evening peaks dearer
- Draft amendment of March 2026 proposes charges above 5 kW and storage above 500 kW; check whether it has been notified

**Where we fit:** We handle the net-metering application, the DISCOM inspection and, for larger plants, the electrical inspector's (CEIG) approval.

[Read the full guide](https://lotussunenergy.com/net-metering-india/)[Source: Mercom India](https://www.mercomindia.com/government-proposes-amendments-to-electricity-consumer-rights-rules)

Consumers of 100 kW and more

### Green Energy Open Access

In force; state charges vary

- Buy green power from an off-site plant from 100 kW of load (down from 1 MW); captive consumers have no minimum
- Connections in the same electricity division can be aggregated (2023 amendment)
- Single-window applications on the national GOAR portal, with deemed approval if not decided in time
- The ISTS charges waiver ended for projects commissioned after 30 June 2025 and is phasing out in steps

**Where we fit:** Captive and open-access plants are usually ground-mount plants: we can take on the piling, civil works, fencing and installation & commissioning.

[Read the full guide](https://lotussunenergy.com/green-energy-open-access/)[Source: GOAR portal](https://greenopenaccess.in/)

Projects covered by the ALMM order

### ALMM List-I and List-II

In force from 1 June 2026

- List-I sets which solar modules may be used in covered projects
- From 1 June 2026, List-II for solar cells applies: covered projects need List-I modules made with List-II cells
- Exemptions for projects whose bid deadline was before the amendment, and for net-metering and open-access projects commissioned before 1 June 2026
- A List-III for wafers is reported for June 2028

**Where we fit:** We do not manufacture modules, so we specify the ALMM-listed or client-approved makes each project needs and keep the documents.

[Read the full guide](https://lotussunenergy.com/almm-list-ii-solar-cells/)[Source: PIB](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2082901)

Anyone importing equipment

### Customs duty on modules and cells

In force

- Budget 2025-26: BCD on modules cut to 20% with a 20% AIDC (about 40% combined); on cells to 20% with 7.5% AIDC
- Budget 2026-27 left the headline rates unchanged and removed duty on a solar-glass input
- Anti-dumping duty on Chinese-origin cells and modules recommended in September 2025; check the current notification

**Where we fit:** For most home, business and scheme projects the route is now Indian ALMM modules; we compare options and paperwork before you commit.

[Read the full guide](https://lotussunenergy.com/solar-import-duty-india/)[Source: Energetica India](https://www.energetica-india.net/news/union-budget-2025-26-solar-cells-and-modules-duty-cut-to-20-percent)

Every plant: modules, inverters, batteries

### BIS Quality Control Order

In force

- Solar Systems, Devices and Components Goods Order, 2025, notified 27 January 2025
- Modules, solar inverters and storage batteries must meet Indian Standards and carry the BIS mark
- Inverters above 200 kW given extra time on self-certification, reportedly to the end of 2026

**Where we fit:** We check BIS and ALMM documents for every component on site and hand them over with the test reports.

[Read the full guide](https://lotussunenergy.com/solar-quality-standards-bis-cea/)[Source: PIB](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2097219)

Utility tenders and large prosumers

### Storage with solar

Advisory for future tenders

- Power Ministry advisory (Feb 2025): two-hour co-located storage equal to 10% of capacity in future solar tenders
- Viability gap funding for battery storage; a second tranche of about Rs 5,400 crore announced in 2025
- ISTS waiver for co-located BESS commissioned by 30 June 2028

**Where we fit:** We can add batteries where backup matters; for most homes and businesses a grid-connected system sized to daytime use pays back fastest.

[Read the full guide](https://lotussunenergy.com/battery-storage-with-solar/)[Source: pv magazine India](https://www.pv-magazine-india.com/2025/02/20/power-ministry-mandates-co-locating-energy-storage-with-solar-projects/)

Legal

# Privacy Policy

What we collect through our forms, why, who processes it, how long we keep it, your rights under India's DPDP Act, and how to reach our Grievance Officer.

Last updated: 11 October 2026

## 1. Who we are

This website is run by **Lotus Sun Energy** ("we", "us"), Pakhanaha Sriram, Muzaffarpur, Bihar 843109, India. We decide how the personal data described here is used, so we are its data fiduciary under India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (DPDP Act). Contact: [info@lotussunenergy.com](mailto:info@lotussunenergy.com).

## 2. What we collect

We collect personal data only when you choose to contact us. Our contact forms ask for:

- **Name**, **phone number** and **email address** (required), so we can reply;
- **Property type**, **city or town** and **average monthly bill** (optional), so we can understand your needs;
- **Message** (optional): whatever you choose to tell us.

Our [free solar quote](https://lotussunenergy.com/free-solar-quote/) form also asks about your project, so we can prepare a proposal: who the system is for, the services you need, how you would like to pay, the site's state, city, type and area, your electricity bill, tariff, connection type, sanctioned load and backup, when you want to start, whether you own the roof or land, your role, and how and when you prefer to be contacted. It also records which website or campaign link brought you to the form, and an indicative system size and savings estimate worked out in your browser from your bill.

The savings calculator on our home page works entirely in your browser: what you type into it is not sent to us. If you email us directly, we receive your email address and whatever your email contains. We do not run user accounts, advertising or tracking of individuals. Like every website host, our host keeps short-lived technical server logs (such as IP address, browser type and the page requested) to deliver the site and keep it secure.

## 3. Why we use it

We use your details **only to answer your enquiry**: to reply, arrange a site visit, discuss your project and, if you ask, prepare a quotation. We rely on the consent you give by submitting the form (DPDP Act, section 6). The quote form gives each request a simple label (Hot, Warm or Cold), worked out in your browser from your bill, start timeline, role and roof ownership, so our team can decide whom to call first. It is never used to refuse a quote: every enquiry is answered by a person.

## 4. Who processes it for us

We use these service providers (data processors), each only to provide its service to us:

- **FormSubmit** (formsubmit.co) receives what you type into our forms and forwards it to our mailbox. See the [FormSubmit privacy policy](https://formsubmit.co/privacy.pdf).
- Our **email provider** hosts our mailbox, [info@lotussunenergy.com](mailto:info@lotussunenergy.com), where enquiries are stored.
- **Cloudflare** (Cloudflare Pages) hosts and delivers this website, protects it from attacks and keeps the technical server logs described above. If we switch on Cloudflare Web Analytics, it counts visits in aggregate without cookies and without identifying you. See the [Cloudflare privacy policy](https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/).

If you go ahead with a project, we share the details the scheme or your DISCOM requires (for example your name, address, electricity connection and bank details for the PM Surya Ghar subsidy) with the national portal and your DISCOM, only to process your application. These providers may process data on servers outside India under their own safeguards. We share your data with no one else, except where the law requires it, or where you ask us to (for example with a bank, if you ask us to help with a solar loan).

## 5. Cookies

**Lotus Sun Energy sets no cookies** and uses no advertising, remarketing or tracking of its own. Our fonts, images and scripts are served from our own site, not from third-party networks. Our host, Cloudflare, may set a strictly necessary security cookie (such as __cf_bm) to tell real visitors from bots; it is not used for advertising and expires within hours. The savings calculator stores nothing on your device.

## 6. How long we keep it

We keep an enquiry for as long as we need it to respond and, if a project follows, for the life of that project and its warranties. Enquiries that do not lead to a project are deleted within 24 months of our last contact with you. Records the law requires us to keep longer, such as tax and accounting records, are kept for the period the law sets.

## 7. No sale, no sharing, no marketing lists

**We never sell your personal data, and we never share it for advertising.** Submitting a form **never subscribes you to a newsletter or marketing list**.

## 8. Your rights

You can ask us to:

- tell you what personal data we hold about you and how we use it;
- correct or complete it;
- delete it;

Frequently Asked Questions

# Your Solar Questions, Answered

Cost, subsidy, EMIs, roofs, net metering, the monsoon and maintenance: everything people ask us before they go solar.

## Cost and savings

How much does rooftop solar cost for a home in India?

As a guide, a home rooftop system costs roughly Rs 55,000 to Rs 65,000 per kW before subsidy, depending on the roof, the structure height and the components. A typical 3 kW home system therefore costs about Rs 1.7 to 2 lakh, and the PM Surya Ghar subsidy brings Rs 78,000 of that back. Use our [savings calculator](https://lotussunenergy.com/#calculator) for your own numbers; the exact price comes after a free site visit.

How much will I save on my electricity bill?

Most homes that size the system to their usage cut their bill by 70 to 90%. Each kW of panels makes roughly 4 units a day on average in most of India (about 1,400 to 1,500 units a year), so at Rs 7 to 8 a unit a 3 kW system saves around Rs 2,500 to 3,000 a month.

How long does solar take to pay for itself?

For a home with the subsidy, typically 3 to 5 years. Businesses without the subsidy usually see 3 to 6 years, depending on the tariff and how much of the power is used during the day. After that the system keeps generating for 25 years or more.

What size of system do I need?

A quick rule: bills around Rs 1,000 to 2,500 a month suit 1 to 2 kW, Rs 2,500 to 4,500 suit about 3 kW, and bills above Rs 5,000 need 5 kW or more. We confirm the size from your bills, sanctioned load and roof during the site visit.

## Subsidy and finance

What government subsidy can I get for home solar?

Under [PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana](https://lotussunenergy.com/pm-surya-ghar-subsidy/) the central subsidy is Rs 30,000 per kW for the first 2 kW and Rs 18,000 for the 3rd kW: Rs 30,000 for 1 kW, Rs 60,000 for 2 kW and Rs 78,000 for 3 kW or more. Housing societies get Rs 18,000 per kW for common facilities. Some states add their own top-up.

Who is eligible for the PM Surya Ghar subsidy?

A household with its own electricity connection, a suitable roof it owns, and no earlier solar subsidy on the same connection. The system must be grid-connected with net metering and use Indian-made (DCR) modules, installed by a vendor registered on the portal.

Do you handle the subsidy paperwork?

Yes. We register you on the national portal, file the DISCOM feasibility and net-metering application, arrange the inspection after installation and follow the claim until the subsidy reaches your bank account.

Can I pay in EMIs?

Yes. Banks offer solar loans, and for home systems up to 3 kW the scheme provides collateral-free loans at around 7% interest. In many cases the EMI is close to the bill it replaces, so you save from the first month. We guide you through the paperwork.

Do businesses get any benefit?

Businesses do not get the PM Surya Ghar subsidy, but a business that owns its plant can usually claim [accelerated depreciation](https://lotussunenergy.com/accelerated-depreciation-solar/), and GST on solar modules is 5%. Ask your chartered accountant to confirm.

## Your roof and site

Is my roof suitable for solar?

Most are. You need roughly 80 to 100 sq ft of shade-free roof per kW, facing south, east or west, without tall trees or buildings shading it between 9 AM and 4 PM. RCC and metal-sheet roofs both work; we check the strength and shade on the site visit.

Will the panels damage my roof or cause leaks?

No. On RCC roofs we use raised structures on concrete or chemically anchored bases with waterproofing at each fixing; on metal sheets we use clamps or sealed fixings matched to the sheet profile. The structure is designed for the wind speed of your area.

I live in a rented house or flat. Can I still go solar?

The subsidy needs a roof the applicant owns. In an apartment, the housing society can install solar for common areas (lifts, pumps, lighting) and claim the society subsidy. Talk to us and we will suggest what is possible.

Do you install ground-mount solar on open land?

Yes. For farms, factories and institutions with spare land we design and build ground-mount plants, including soil checks, pile foundations, structures, fencing and the grid connection. See [ground-mount solar](https://lotussunenergy.com/service-ground-mount/).

## Installation and approvals

How long does installation take?

For a typical home, the physical installation takes 2 to 4 days. The whole process, including portal registration, DISCOM feasibility, net meter and inspection, usually takes a few weeks, depending on your DISCOM.

What is net metering?

A two-way meter records the power you draw from the grid and the surplus solar power you send to it. You pay only for the net units, and summer surplus can offset monsoon months within the settlement period. See our [net metering guide](https://lotussunenergy.com/net-metering-india/).

Does solar work during a power cut?

A standard grid-connected (on-grid) system shuts down during a grid outage for the safety of line workers. If you want power during cuts, choose a hybrid system with batteries; we will explain the cost difference honestly.

Which panels and inverters do you use?

We do not manufacture equipment. We specify BIS-certified, ALMM-listed modules (Indian-made DCR modules where the subsidy needs them) and reliable on-grid or hybrid inverters with monitoring, with the makes and warranties written into your quote.

## Maintenance and performance

Does solar work in the monsoon and in winter?

Yes, at lower output. Panels generate on cloudy days, just less. Over a year the sunny months more than make up for it, and net metering lets you bank the surplus.

How much maintenance does solar need?

Very little: rinse the panels with plain water every 2 to 4 weeks (more often in dusty areas), keep shade-causing branches trimmed, and get a yearly check of the wiring, earthing and inverter. We offer [maintenance plans](https://lotussunenergy.com/service-om/) for larger systems.

How long do solar panels last?

Quality modules come with a 25 to 30 year performance warranty and keep producing well beyond that, losing only a small percentage of output each year. Inverters typically last 10 to 15 years.

## About Lotus Sun Energy

Who is Lotus Sun Energy?

A new, veteran-led solar company from Muzaffarpur, Bihar. We are led by ex-servicemen and bring the same discipline, honesty and commitment that served the nation to powering India's homes and businesses with clean solar energy.

Where do you work?

What services do you offer?

Rooftop solar for homes, societies and businesses; ground-mount plants; turnkey EPC on the CAPEX model; installation and commissioning; pile foundations and civil works; and operation and maintenance.

How do I get a quote?

Fill in the [free quote form](https://lotussunenergy.com/free-solar-quote/), use the [contact form](https://lotussunenergy.com/contact/) or email info@lotussunenergy.com with your location and a recent electricity bill. We reply within one working day and book a free site visit.

Solar Glossary

# Solar Terms, in Plain English

The words you will meet when going solar, from kW and net metering to DISCOM, ALMM and payback.

## A

Accelerated depreciation

A tax benefit that lets a business that owns a solar plant write off its cost faster than normal assets, reducing taxable income in the early years.

ACDB / DCDB

AC and DC distribution boards: the enclosures that house the fuses, isolators and surge protection between the panels, the inverter and the grid connection.

ALMM

Approved List of Models and Manufacturers: the list of solar modules (and, from June 2026, cells) approved by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) for covered projects.

## B

Balance of system (BOS)

Everything in a solar system except the panels: mounting structures, inverters, cables, distribution boards, earthing, lightning protection and monitoring.

Bifacial module

A solar module that generates power from both sides, using light reflected from the roof or ground onto its rear face.

## C

CAPEX model

You pay for the solar system upfront (or with a loan) and own it outright, keeping all the savings.

Commissioning

The final stage of an installation: testing every component, synchronising the system with the grid and handing it over ready to generate.

CUF (capacity utilisation factor)

The energy a system actually generates in a year as a percentage of what it would generate running at full capacity all year.

## D

DCR (domestic content requirement)

A rule in some government schemes, including PM Surya Ghar, that modules and cells must be made in India.

DISCOM

Your electricity distribution company, which approves net metering, installs the bi-directional meter and inspects grid-connected systems.

## E

Earthing

Connecting the system's metal structures and electrical equipment to the ground so that fault currents and lightning are carried safely away.

EMI

Equated monthly instalment: paying for a solar system in fixed monthly amounts through a loan instead of all at once.

EPC

Engineering, procurement and construction: a single contract covering the design, equipment purchase and building of the whole system.

## G

Grid-connected (on-grid) system

A solar system connected to the utility grid, which can draw from or export to the grid; the most common type for homes and businesses.

Ground-mount solar

Panels installed on structures fixed to the ground, typically on pile foundations; used for farms, factories and open land.

## H

Hybrid system

A solar system with batteries that also connects to the grid, so it can keep essential loads running during power cuts.

## I

I&C (installation & commissioning)

The on-site work of building a solar system to an agreed design and bringing it into operation: structures, panels, cabling, inverters, earthing, testing and commissioning.

Inverter

The equipment that converts the direct current (DC) from the panels into alternating current (AC) for use at home or export to the grid.

## K

kW / kWp

Kilowatt and kilowatt-peak: the rated output of a solar system under standard test conditions. A 3 kW home system has about 3 kWp of panels.

kWh (unit)

A kilowatt-hour, the 'unit' on your electricity bill. In most of India, 1 kW of panels makes about 4 units a day on average.

## L

Lightning arrestor

A device that intercepts lightning strikes and conducts them safely to earth, protecting panels and equipment.

## M

MMS (module mounting structure)

The steel or aluminium frame that holds the panels at the designed tilt and height.

## N

National Portal

pmsuryaghar.gov.in, the website where households apply for the PM Surya Ghar subsidy and choose a registered vendor.

Net metering

A billing arrangement where the power your solar system exports to the grid is offset against the power you draw from it.

## O

Off-grid system

A solar system with batteries that is not connected to the grid; used where there is no reliable grid supply.

OPEX / RESCO model

A developer finances and owns the plant on your roof or land, and you buy its power at an agreed tariff for many years.

## P

Payback period

The time it takes for the savings on your electricity bill to equal what you paid for the solar system.

Performance ratio (PR)

Actual energy generated divided by the theoretical energy available from the sunlight; a measure of how well a system is built and maintained.

Pile foundation

A steel or concrete pile driven or cast into the ground to anchor the mounting structures of a ground-mount plant.

PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana

The central government scheme that subsidises rooftop solar for homes: up to Rs 78,000 for a system of 3 kW or more.

## R

Rooftop solar

Panels installed on a building's RCC or metal-sheet roof, turning unused roof space into a power source.

## S

Sanctioned load

The maximum load (in kW or kVA) your DISCOM has approved for your connection; it usually caps the size of a net-metered system.

Shadow analysis

A check of where trees, water tanks, parapets and nearby buildings cast shade on the roof through the day and year, so panels go where the sun is.

## T

Tier-1 module

A module from a large, bankable manufacturer with an established production and financing track record.

TOPCon

Tunnel oxide passivated contact: a high-efficiency solar cell technology now common in new modules.

[Read the FAQ](https://lotussunenergy.com/faq/)[Solar Guides](https://lotussunenergy.com/insights/)

Guide · Schemes

# PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana 2026: Subsidy, Eligibility and How to Apply

India's rooftop solar scheme for homes: up to Rs 78,000 central subsidy, support for housing societies, low-cost loans and the national portal. What you get, who qualifies, and the steps from application to subsidy.

On this page

- What the scheme offers
- Who can apply
- How to apply, step by step
- Getting the most from a home system
- How Lotus Sun Energy helps you claim it
- Frequently asked questions
- Sources

By the [Lotus Sun Energy team](https://lotussunenergy.com/about/) · Updated 11 Oct 2026 · 3 min read

**Key takeaways**

- Central subsidy: **Rs 30,000 for 1 kW, Rs 60,000 for 2 kW, Rs 78,000 for 3 kW or more**
- Housing societies and RWAs get **Rs 18,000 per kW** for common facilities, up to 500 kW
- Approved by the Cabinet on 29 February 2024 with an outlay of **Rs 75,021 crore**; the government's target is 75 lakh households by December 2026, on the way to 1 crore
- Modules must be Indian-made (DCR), installed by a registered vendor, and the application made on the national portal
- Many states add their own top-up subsidy; check your DISCOM

## What the scheme offers

**PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana** was launched by the Prime Minister on 13 February 2024 and approved by the Union Cabinet on 29 February 2024 with an outlay of **Rs 75,021 crore**. It aims to put rooftop solar on one crore homes so that each can generate up to about 300 units a month, and the government's milestone is **75 lakh households by December 2026**.

Central financial assistance under PM Surya Ghar

| Category | Support | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Homes, 1 kW | Rs 30,000 | 60% of benchmark cost for the first 2 kW |
| Homes, 2 kW | Rs 60,000 |  |
| Homes, 3 kW or more | Rs 78,000 (cap) | 40% of the additional cost between 2 and 3 kW; no extra subsidy above 3 kW |
| Housing societies / RWAs (common facilities, EV charging) | Rs 18,000 per kW | Up to 500 kW, at 3 kW per house |
| Special category states and UTs | Higher benchmark support where notified | Including the North-Eastern states |

**Rs 78,000**Maximum central subsidy per home

**1 crore**Homes targeted

**Rs 75,021 cr**Scheme outlay

**~300 units**Free power a month, the aim

## Who can apply

- An Indian household with its own roof suitable for solar panels
- A valid electricity connection in the household's name
- No earlier central subsidy for rooftop solar on the same connection
- Housing societies and RWAs for common loads, through the society

## How to apply, step by step

- **Register**On the national portal (pmsuryaghar.gov.in) with your state, DISCOM, consumer number and mobile number.
- **Apply**Fill in the rooftop solar application; the DISCOM checks feasibility.
- **Choose a registered vendor**Pick a vendor registered with your DISCOM; agree capacity and price.
- **Install**The vendor installs the system with DCR modules and a compliant inverter.
- **Net meter and inspection**Submit plant details, apply for the net meter; the DISCOM inspects and commissions.
- **Subsidy**After the commissioning certificate is generated on the portal, submit bank details; the subsidy is credited to your account.

Collateral-free loans of around 7% are available from public-sector banks for residential systems up to 3 kW, and the portal links to lenders. Model solar villages in each district receive additional support.

## Getting the most from a home system

- Size to your consumption: a 3 kW system typically generates around 12 units a day in most of India, depending on sunshine and orientation.
- Use a shade-free, south-facing area where you can; avoid water tanks and parapets casting shadows.
- Ask for the DCR module certificate, inverter BIS certificate and warranty documents.
- Keep the panels clean: dust can cut output noticeably in dry months (see [O&M and module cleaning](https://lotussunenergy.com/solar-om-module-cleaning/)).

## How Lotus Sun Energy helps you claim it

We take care of the whole process: registration on the national portal, the DISCOM feasibility and net-metering application, a DCR-compliant system sized to your bill, installation, the inspection and the follow-up until the subsidy reaches your bank account. The site visit and the quotation are free.

PM Surya Ghar is for homes and housing societies. For businesses, the equivalent levers are [accelerated depreciation](https://lotussunenergy.com/accelerated-depreciation-solar/), the [5% GST rate](https://lotussunenergy.com/gst-on-solar-india/) and [net metering](https://lotussunenergy.com/net-metering-india/) or [open access](https://lotussunenergy.com/green-energy-open-access/).

Want to know your exact subsidy and system cost? Book a free site visit and we will work it out with you.

[Get a free solar quote](https://lotussunenergy.com/free-solar-quote/)

## Frequently asked questions

How much subsidy do I get under PM Surya Ghar?

Rs 30,000 for 1 kW, Rs 60,000 for 2 kW and Rs 78,000 for 3 kW or more. Housing societies get Rs 18,000 per kW for common facilities up to 500 kW.

Can a business get the PM Surya Ghar subsidy?

No. The scheme is for residential households and housing societies. Businesses benefit instead from accelerated depreciation, 5% GST and net metering or open access.

Do I need Indian-made panels?

Yes. Systems under the scheme must use domestically manufactured (DCR) modules and be installed by a vendor registered with your DISCOM.

How long does the subsidy take?

After installation, inspection and net-meter commissioning, the commissioning certificate is generated on the portal and the subsidy is paid to your bank account, typically within weeks.

Guide · Market Update

# India's Solar Capacity in 2026: 171 GW and What It Means for Your Business

MNRE data put India's solar fleet at 171.05 GW on 30 September 2026. Where the growth is, why rooftop and C&I solar are surging, and how to plan a plant in a crowded market.

On this page

- The numbers in one place
- Why India is building so fast
- Where the growth is coming from
- What this means if you are planning a plant
- How Lotus Sun Energy can help
- Frequently asked questions
- Sources

By the [Lotus Sun Energy team](https://lotussunenergy.com/about/) · Updated 11 Oct 2026 · 4 min read

**Key takeaways**

- India had **171.05 GW** of solar on 30 September 2026, per MNRE's physical-progress data
- That is about 30 GW more than the 140.6 GW MNRE reported for January 2026
- Grid-connected rooftop solar has reached 33.41 GW; ground-mounted plants make up 125.65 GW
- Renewables including large hydro total about 299 GW (about 247 GW excluding large hydro), on the road to 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030
- The scarce resource is now skilled installation and commissioning: book your EPC partner and approvals early

## The numbers in one place

India's solar build-out keeps setting records. The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) publishes cumulative installed capacity every month, and its table for **30 September 2026** shows **171.05 GW** of solar. That is up from 150.26 GW on 31 March 2026 and 164.59 GW on 31 July 2026, and roughly 30 GW more than the 140.6 GW MNRE reported for January 2026.

**171.05 GW**Solar installed, 30 Sep 2026

**125.65 GW**Ground-mounted plants

**33.41 GW**Grid-connected rooftop

**~299 GW**Renewable capacity incl. large hydro (MNRE)

India's solar capacity by segment, cumulative as on 30 September 2026 (MNRE)

| Segment | Installed capacity | What it covers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ground-mounted solar | 125.65 GW | Utility-scale parks and open-access or captive plants on land |
| Grid-connected rooftop | 33.41 GW | Homes, factories, warehouses, institutions and commercial buildings |
| Hybrid projects (solar part) | 5.36 GW | Solar in wind-solar hybrid projects |
| Off-grid solar | 6.63 GW | Solar pumps, mini-grids and standalone systems |
| Total solar | 171.05 GW | All of the above |

Two trends stand out. Rooftop solar, long the laggard, has accelerated sharply thanks to PM Surya Ghar for homes and to factories and commercial buildings cutting their power bills. And ground-mounted plants keep growing through utility tenders and through companies building captive and open-access plants for their own use.

## Why India is building so fast

The direction is set at the highest level. At COP26 in Glasgow in 2021 the Prime Minister announced the **Panchamrit** commitments, the first of which is **500 GW of non-fossil electricity capacity by 2030**. Non-fossil sources passed half of India's installed power capacity in June 2025, five years ahead of the original goal.

Policy then makes solar cheaper and easier to adopt:

- **GST on solar equipment fell from 12% to 5%** from 22 September 2025, lowering the upfront cost of every plant (see [our GST guide](https://lotussunenergy.com/gst-on-solar-india/)).
- **Accelerated depreciation** lets a business that owns its plant write off the cost quickly (see [depreciation explained](https://lotussunenergy.com/accelerated-depreciation-solar/)).
- **PM Surya Ghar** subsidises rooftop solar for homes and **PM-KUSUM** solarises farms and feeders.
- **Green Energy Open Access** rules let consumers with as little as 100 kW of load buy green power from plants elsewhere.
- **ALMM** and import duties steer buyers towards Indian-made modules and, since 1 June 2026, Indian-made cells.

For a business the economics are now simple: a well-built plant on your own roof or land produces power for 25 years at a cost per unit well below most commercial and industrial grid tariffs, and the cost of the plant is recovered in a few years.

## Where the growth is coming from

### Utility-scale parks and tenders

Large solar parks tendered by SECI and the states still account for most new megawatts. New tenders increasingly ask for co-located battery storage (see [storage with solar](https://lotussunenergy.com/battery-storage-with-solar/)).

### Commercial and industrial (C&I) rooftops

Factories with large sheet roofs are among the best sites in the country: the roof already exists, consumption is during the day and tariffs are high. Shops, offices, schools and hospitals follow the same logic on a smaller scale.

### Homes and housing societies

Home rooftops are the fastest-growing segment by number of systems. The PM Surya Ghar subsidy (up to Rs 78,000 for a home) and collateral-free loans have brought rooftop solar within reach of ordinary families (see the [PM Surya Ghar guide](https://lotussunenergy.com/pm-surya-ghar-subsidy/)).

### Farms and agro-industry

Farms, cold stores, rice and flour mills and other agro-industries with daytime load and spare land are building ground-mount plants, and PM-KUSUM supports solar pumps and feeder-level plants (see [PM-KUSUM](https://lotussunenergy.com/pm-kusum-scheme/)).

## What this means if you are planning a plant

Record volumes are good news for prices and choice, but they create bottlenecks in three places:

- **Skilled installation crews.** Experienced installation & commissioning teams, piling rigs and supervisors are booked months ahead in the peak season.
- **Approvals.** DISCOM feasibility, net-metering or open-access approval and the Electrical Inspector's (CEIG) inspection all take time, and queues grow when everyone builds at once.
- **Compliant equipment.** ALMM-listed modules (with List-II cells for covered projects) and BIS-certified inverters must be specified and documented from the start.

The practical answer is to start early and choose a partner who is transparent about the design, the components and the paperwork, and who puts it all in writing. Our checklist of [12 questions to ask a solar EPC](https://lotussunenergy.com/choose-solar-epc-partner/) is a good place to start.

Planning a rooftop or ground-mount system for 2026-27? We will size it, cost it and map the approvals for you.

We offer free site visits across India from our office in Muzaffarpur, Bihar.

## Frequently asked questions

How much solar capacity does India have in 2026?

MNRE's physical-progress data show 171.05 GW of solar installed as on 30 September 2026: 125.65 GW ground-mounted, 33.41 GW grid-connected rooftop, 5.36 GW in hybrid projects and 6.63 GW off-grid.

What is India's renewable energy target for 2030?

500 GW of non-fossil fuel electricity capacity by 2030, the first of the Panchamrit commitments the Prime Minister announced at COP26 in 2021.

Is it a good time for a business to install solar?

For most commercial and industrial consumers, yes: GST on solar equipment is 5%, a business owner can claim accelerated depreciation, and a well-built plant generates for 25 years at a cost per unit below typical C&I tariffs. Book installation crews and approvals early because demand is high.

Where can I check the latest official solar figures?

MNRE publishes cumulative installed capacity every month on its physical-progress page (mnre.gov.in). PIB press releases summarise the milestones.

Guide · Tax

# GST on Solar in India (2026): 5% on Equipment, About 8.9% on EPC Contracts

The GST Council cut GST on solar devices from 12% to 5% from 22 September 2025. How it applies to modules, inverters and full EPC contracts, what the 70:30 rule means, and how much a plant saves.

On this page

- What changed and when
- How GST works on a full EPC contract: the 70:30 rule
- Input tax credit: can your business claim the GST back?
- Worked example: what the cut saves on a Rs 1 crore plant
- Other taxes that affect a solar project
- Frequently asked questions
- Sources

By the [Lotus Sun Energy team](https://lotussunenergy.com/about/) · Updated 11 Oct 2026 · 4 min read

**Key takeaways**

- GST on solar cells, modules and specified renewable-energy devices is **5%**, cut from 12% with effect from **22 September 2025**
- For a solar plant supplied with installation services, a deemed **70% goods : 30% services** split applies, which works out to about **8.9%** overall
- The Andhra Pradesh High Court (December 2025) upheld the 70:30 method for a solar EPC contract and set aside an 18% assessment
- A business using the plant for taxable supplies can usually claim input tax credit: confirm with your tax adviser
- On a Rs 1 crore plant the cut is worth roughly Rs 2.5 lakh to Rs 4.9 lakh, depending on how the contract is structured

## What changed and when

At its **56th meeting on 3 September 2025**, the GST Council cut the rate on solar cells, solar modules and other renewable-energy devices from **12% to 5%**, effective **22 September 2025**. It was part of a wider rate rationalisation, and for solar it reversed the increase from 5% to 12% made in 2021.

Because equipment is the largest part of what a solar plant costs, the cut flows almost directly into a lower project price and a shorter payback.

GST on common solar items after 22 September 2025

| Item | Typical HSN | GST rate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Solar PV cells and modules | 8541 | 5% |
| Solar power generators and specified parts (as listed in the rate notification), such as grid-tie inverters for solar systems | 8501 / 8504 | 5% where covered by the solar-devices entry |
| Installation, civil and electrical services supplied on their own | 9954 / 9987 | 18% |
| Solar plant supplied with services (EPC), deemed split | Mixed | 70% at 5% + 30% at 18% = about 8.9% |

**Check the exact entry**

Whether a particular component (structures, cables, batteries, monitoring hardware) falls under the 5% solar-devices entry depends on the wording of the rate notification and how the item is supplied. Your supplier's invoice and your tax adviser should agree on the HSN.

## How GST works on a full EPC contract: the 70:30 rule

Most plants are bought as a package: modules, inverters, structures and cables plus the design, installation and commissioning. Since 2019 the GST rules have deemed such a supply of a solar power generating system with services to be **70% goods and 30% services**. The goods part is taxed at the solar rate and the services part at 18%.

Effective GST on a solar EPC contract under the 70:30 rule

| Period | Goods (70%) | Services (30%) | Effective rate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Before 1 Oct 2021 | 5% | 18% | 8.9% |
| 1 Oct 2021 to 21 Sep 2025 | 12% | 18% | 13.8% |
| From 22 Sep 2025 | 5% | 18% | 8.9% |

Tax officers have sometimes argued that a solar EPC contract is a works contract for immovable property taxable at 18% in full. In **December 2025 the Andhra Pradesh High Court**, in a case brought by a module maker and EPC company, held that the 70:30 formula applies to such a contract and directed the tax to be recomputed at about 8.9%. The judgment is binding only in that state, but it is persuasive elsewhere.

**Our practice**

We set out supply and services clearly in every CAPEX contract and invoice them in line with the applicable rule, so the tax treatment is transparent from the quotation onwards.

## Input tax credit: can your business claim the GST back?

A registered business that uses the solar plant in the course of making taxable supplies (a factory, a warehouse, a mill selling flour) can generally claim input tax credit on the GST paid on the plant, treating it as a capital good. That makes the GST itself largely a cash-flow item rather than a cost.

Credit can be restricted where the power is used for exempt supplies, where the plant is treated as immovable property under your facts, or where the books treat it in a particular way. The rules are nuanced, so confirm the position for your business with your chartered accountant before you budget the project.

## Worked example: what the cut saves on a Rs 1 crore plant

Take a commercial plant whose pre-tax contract value is **Rs 1 crore**.

GST payable on a Rs 1 crore solar EPC contract (illustrative)

| Scenario | Rate applied | GST before the cut | GST after the cut | Saving |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| EPC contract, 70:30 rule | 13.8% to 8.9% | Rs 13.8 lakh | Rs 8.9 lakh | Rs 4.9 lakh |
| Equipment only (installation billed separately) | 12% to 5% on Rs 70 lakh | Rs 8.4 lakh | Rs 3.5 lakh | Rs 4.9 lakh |
| Modules only (about 35-40% of cost) | 12% to 5% on Rs 37.5 lakh | Rs 4.5 lakh | Rs 1.9 lakh | Rs 2.6 lakh |

For a business that cannot claim input tax credit, the saving is a straight reduction in project cost. For one that can, it reduces the cash locked up until the credit is used. Either way, payback improves.

Want a quotation with the 5% rate and the 70:30 split shown line by line? Tell us about your site.

[Get a free solar quote](https://lotussunenergy.com/free-solar-quote/)

## Other taxes that affect a solar project

- **Customs duty** on imported cells and modules (see [solar import duty in 2026](https://lotussunenergy.com/solar-import-duty-india/)).
- **Accelerated depreciation** on the plant for a business owner (see [our depreciation guide](https://lotussunenergy.com/accelerated-depreciation-solar/)).
- **Electricity duty** on self-consumed power, which some states levy or waive for captive solar under their solar policies.
- **Open-access charges** if the plant is off-site (see [Green Energy Open Access](https://lotussunenergy.com/green-energy-open-access/)).

## Frequently asked questions

What is the GST rate on solar panels in 2026?

5%. The GST Council cut the rate on solar cells, modules and other specified renewable-energy devices from 12% to 5% with effect from 22 September 2025.

What is the GST on a solar EPC contract?

Where a solar power generating system is supplied with installation services, 70% of the value is treated as goods (5%) and 30% as services (18%), an effective rate of about 8.9%.

Is the 70:30 rule upheld by the courts?

In December 2025 the Andhra Pradesh High Court held that the 70:30 formula applies to a solar EPC contract and set aside an 18% assessment. It is binding in Andhra Pradesh and persuasive elsewhere.

Can my company claim input tax credit on a solar plant?

Usually yes, if the plant is used in making taxable supplies and is treated as a capital good in your books. Restrictions can apply, so confirm with your chartered accountant.

Does GST apply to O&M and module cleaning services?

Yes. Standalone services such as operation and maintenance or module cleaning are generally taxed at 18%.

Guide · Policy

# ALMM List-I and List-II Explained: The Made-in-India Rule for Solar Modules and Cells

MNRE's Approved List of Models and Manufacturers now covers solar cells as well as modules. What List-I and List-II mean, which projects they bind, the exemptions, and how to stay compliant.

On this page

- What ALMM is and why it exists
- List-I and List-II side by side
- Which projects must comply
- What it means for price and supply
- How to check compliance before you order
- Frequently asked questions
- Sources

By the [Lotus Sun Energy team](https://lotussunenergy.com/about/) · Updated 11 Oct 2026 · 3 min read

**Key takeaways**

- ALMM List-I covers solar **modules**; List-II, for solar **cells**, applies from **1 June 2026**
- Covered projects must use List-I modules that are themselves made with List-II cells
- Projects whose bid deadline fell on or before the amendment are exempt from the cell requirement; net-metering and open-access projects commissioned before 1 June 2026 were exempted too
- MNRE has signalled a third list, for wafers, later in the decade (reported for June 2028)
- Ask for the ALMM listing, the model number and the cell source in writing before you order modules

## What ALMM is and why it exists

The **Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM)** is a register kept by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy. Only the module models and manufacturers on it may be used in the projects the ALMM Order covers. MNRE issued the order in 2019 to make sure that solar plants built with public support or for public utilities use reliable equipment from verified factories, and to build up manufacturing in India.

Until 2026 the order had one list, **List-I for solar PV modules**. MNRE then amended the ALMM Order 2019 to add **List-II for solar PV cells**, with effect from **1 June 2026**.

## List-I and List-II side by side

The ALMM lists in 2026

| List | Covers | In force from | What a covered project must do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| List-I | Solar PV modules (model and factory) | 2021 (original order of 2019) | Use only modules from List-I |
| List-II | Solar PV cells (manufacturer and factory) | 1 June 2026 | Use List-I modules made with List-II cells |
| List-III (signalled) | Wafers | Reported for June 2028; not yet in force | Watch for MNRE's notification |

In practice List-II means that a covered project needs modules whose **cells were also made in an ALMM-listed Indian factory**. A module assembled in India from imported cells stays on List-I but no longer satisfies a project that needs List-II cells.

## Which projects must comply

The order applies to projects set out in it, chiefly:

- Government and government-assisted projects, including those under central schemes
- Projects selling power to the government or to DISCOMs, such as plants built under central or state tenders
- Projects under schemes that require it, such as PM-KUSUM and PM Surya Ghar (which already insist on domestic-content modules)
- Net-metering and open-access projects, which MNRE has brought within the order's scope, subject to the exemptions below

### The exemptions

- Projects whose **bid submission deadline was on or before the date of the List-II amendment** are excused from the cell requirement, though they still need List-I modules.
- Net-metering and open-access projects **commissioned before 1 June 2026** were exempt from sourcing List-II cells.

**Purely private captive plants**

Whether a privately funded captive plant must use ALMM modules depends on how it connects and sells power, and on your state's rules. Many clients choose ALMM equipment anyway for quality and future flexibility. Check the position for your project before ordering.

## What it means for price and supply

Indian cell capacity is growing quickly but is smaller than module capacity, so modules with domestic cells (often called DCR modules) carry a premium over modules with imported cells. Lead times can also be longer in peak months.

Plan for it: fix the module specification at the design stage, get written confirmation of the ALMM listing and cell source from the supplier, and lock delivery dates into the project schedule.

## How to check compliance before you order

- **Find the list**Download the current List-I and List-II from MNRE's ALMM pages; the lists are updated regularly.
- **Match the model**Check the exact module model number, wattage and factory address against List-I.
- **Trace the cells**Ask the module maker for the cell manufacturer and factory, and check it against List-II.
- **Keep the paper trail**Keep invoices, the ALMM extract and the maker's declaration. DISCOMs, scheme portals and inspectors can ask for them.
- **Inspect on delivery**Match nameplates and serial numbers on site with the documents before installation starts.

Lotus Sun Energy does not manufacture modules or inverters. We specify ALMM-listed (and, where the subsidy needs it, DCR) makes, and we check and record what arrives on site, so the documents are ready when the DISCOM or inspector asks.

## Frequently asked questions

What is ALMM List-II?

The list of approved solar cell manufacturers, added to MNRE's ALMM Order 2019. From 1 June 2026 covered projects must use List-I modules that are made with List-II cells.

Is ALMM mandatory for rooftop solar?

It is mandatory for projects covered by the order, including scheme-backed rooftop solar such as PM Surya Ghar. For other rooftop plants it depends on the connection and the state rules; many owners choose ALMM equipment anyway.

What are DCR modules?

Domestic Content Requirement modules: modules made with Indian cells. Schemes such as PM Surya Ghar and PM-KUSUM require them.

Will there be an ALMM list for wafers?

MNRE has signalled a List-III for wafers, reported for June 2028. It is not yet in force; watch for the notification.
